slides:
ClaimMap
- Know what a deal rests on, before and during the pitch
- Hackathon build, 14 Nov 2026
- Team: Nurassyl Serikov (CS, City University of Hong Kong)

Problem
- VCs spend 118 hours on due diligence per deal on average (survey of 885 VCs, Gompers et al. 2020)
- Experienced investors say every pitch contains at least three or four common lies (Kawasaki and
Reichert, 2006)
- A deal usually rests on a few load-bearing claims, but decks list dozens

Solution
- Claim map: every deck claim, checked with arithmetic and web evidence, ranked by how much of the
deal rests on it
- Live mode: transcribes the pitch and flags drift from the deck about 4-6 seconds after it is said
- One-page investment memo and a 0-100 ClaimMap Score with cited criteria

Competition
- GoPresent and TechTruth check deck claims and return flat lists of verdicts
- Faktum and VeriFact fact-check spoken claims live, one sentence at a time
- None of them compares the live pitch with the founder's own deck or ranks which claims the deal rests
on

Traction
- Built in one day at this hackathon
- Tested on 3 founder-published decks and 8 TechCrunch Startup Battlefield final pitches
- 0 paying customers so far

Business model
- Per-seat subscription for funds, free tier for angels
- Reference price: TechTruth charges VC funds 799 EUR for a beta trial

Ask
- 2-3 funds to pilot ClaimMap on their next 10 decks

title: ClaimMap (our own pitch deck)

brief.headline: Dig deeper: the deck misstates its two closest competitors, and the core product claims (checking every claim, flagging drift in 4-6 seconds) have no evidence behind them yet.
brief.summary: ClaimMap is a hackathon-built tool that checks every deck claim with arithmetic and web evidence, ranks claims by how much the deal rests on them, and flags drift live 4-6 seconds after it is said. It asks 2-3 funds to pilot it on their next 10 decks. The claim that GoPresent and TechTruth only return flat verdict lists is contradicted by their own sites: GoPresent produces IC-memo drafts, gap lists and coaching, and TechTruth a 9-chapter report with founder checks and benchmarking. The claim that Faktum and VeriFact fact-check speech live holds up, and the TechTruth EUR 799 beta price is confirmed. The differentiation claim (nobody compares the live pitch to the deck and ranks load-bearing claims) is plausible but unproven, and PitchBob has announced a similar live-delta feature. Nothing about the product's accuracy, latency or test results is verified, and there are 0 paying customers. We reviewed the deck only, so none of this has been tested live.
strengths: Targets a real workflow gap: no shipped product found that both compares the live pitch to the deck and ranks load-bearing claims
Pricing reference is accurate: TechTruth's EUR 799 beta trial for VC funds is confirmed, which gives a benchmark for monetization
The ask is small and concrete: a pilot on 10 decks per fund, and the founder discloses 0 paying customers
Claims about live-speech checking by Faktum and VeriFact are accurate, so the team knows the landscape in part

red_flags.text: The deck's description of its closest competitors is wrong. GoPresent and TechTruth go beyond flat verdict lists (memos, gap lists, coaching, a 9-chapter report with founder checks and benchmarking), so the positioning is overstated and the 'no competitor' story is weaker.

The differentiation claim is unproven and at risk. PitchBob has announced a 'Live Pitch vs. Deck Delta' feature, and Faktum and VeriFact already check speech live. The edge could be a feature one competitor ships within a quarter.

The central product claims have no evidence: checking every claim with arithmetic and web evidence, ranking by deal load, and a 4-6 second drift flag. No latency measurement, precision/recall figures or false-positive rates were provided.
The traction is only an internal test on 3 founder decks and 8 Battlefield pitches. No public source confirms it, and there is no ground truth showing that the flags or the ranking were correct.
No customers or commitments: the ask is a pilot with no named funds, LOIs or success criteria, and the per-seat pricing model is untested. The product was built in one day at a hackathon.

questions: GoPresent and TechTruth already offer IC memos, gap lists and founder checks. What can ClaimMap do that they can't, and is it more than a feature gap?
What stops PitchBob, Faktum or VeriFact from shipping live deck-vs-pitch comparison and claim ranking within a quarter? What is the defensible edge in ranking?
What is the end-to-end drift-flag latency on a real pitch, and what are the precision, recall and false-positive rates?
Which 11 decks and pitches were tested, what did ClaimMap flag, and how was correctness of the flags and the load ranking judged?
Do any funds have conversations, LOIs or pilot commitments, and what would make a fund pay per seat after the pilot?
evidence_requests: Side-by-side outputs of ClaimMap, GoPresent and TechTruth on the same deck, with a feature matrix and screenshots
Screen recording with timestamps of a live run on a real pitch, plus a latency log
List of the 11 test items with ClaimMap outputs, ground-truth labels and a precision/recall table
Technical description of the load-bearing ranking method and any validation against investor judgment
Names of funds in conversation, any LOIs or pilot agreements, and the pilot success criteria and pricing assumptions
